title: Does the Zoo stay a dev tool, or become something players get?
question: You asked for a way to see all the new creatures in action, and the Zoo delivered: a debug door on the title screen opening onto a flat field with a button per species, each spawning the way its real lifecycle does. What it accidentally became is close to a field guide — picture, name, and the animal doing its thing. Phase 1's players will meet each critter exactly once, at speed, in the middle of something else.
why_now: Cheap to decide now, before anyone builds on the wrong assumption. Nothing is foreclosed either way — the roster builds itself from the species table, so a player-facing version is just a different door onto the same list.

options.label: Keep it a dev tool for now
options.detail: Nothing to build, nothing to teach. Revisit as a player feature when the critters have actually debuted in real games.

options.label: A bestiary that fills in
options.detail: A collection page where a species appears only after the player has met it in a real game. Strong pull for a kid; costs one set of saved flags. Best considered at the next milestone.

options.label: Ship the sandbox to players
options.detail: Cheapest to ship, but it hands players the answer to every pest before the pest is a question — against the meet-things-in-order pacing.
